intro: In positive sentences, must and have to are very similar. But in the negative, they have opposite meanings: “mustn't” = it is not allowed; “don't have to” = it is not necessary, you can choose. Mixing them up can cause real misunderstandings.
objectifs: Say that something is not allowed with mustn't (and can't / not allowed to).
Say that something is not necessary with don't / doesn't have to (and needn't).
Choose the right form for the meaning you want.
Talk about no obligation in the past with didn't have to.

texte: “Mustn't” (must not) means an action is not allowed: don't do it. It is a prohibition, often a rule or a warning.
“Don't have to” means an action is not necessary: you can do it if you want, but you don't need to. It is a freedom, not a prohibition.

lignes: She doesn't have to work today.

exemples: You mustn't be late for the exam.
A warning: being late is not OK.
You don't have to be early. Ten o'clock is fine.
Not necessary: you can come at ten.

texte: Many learners think “don't have to” means “it is not allowed”. It doesn't! It means “it is not necessary”.
If a sign says “You don't have to pay”, it means it is free — not that paying is forbidden!
exemples: You don't have to touch the screen — it works with your voice.
We don't have to get up early tomorrow. It's Sunday!

texte: “Can't” and “be not allowed to” also express prohibition, especially when the rule comes from outside (a law, official rules). “Mustn't” is common for a personal warning or very strong advice.
In conversation, “can't” is often more natural than “mustn't” for a rule: “You can't park here”.
exemples: You can't park here. It's for buses.
Children aren't allowed to swim without an adult.
You mustn't tell anyone. It's a secret!

texte: In British English, “needn't + base” means the same as “don't have to”: “You needn't bring anything”. “Don't need to” is also very common.
In the past, prohibition uses “couldn't” or “wasn't / weren't allowed to” (mustn't has no past form). No obligation uses “didn't have to”.

lignes: You mustn't / can't use your phone.
We couldn't / weren't allowed to use our phones.
I don't have to wear a tie.
I didn't have to wear a tie.

formule: mustn't + base = not allowed · don't / doesn't have to + base = not necessary
prononciation: “mustn't” is /ˈmʌsnt/: the first t is silent. Don't say “must-ent”.
“don't have to”: /dəʊnt ˈhæf tə/ (UK), with an f; “doesn't have to” /ˈdʌznt ˈhæf tə/.
For a prohibition, stress “mustn't”: You MUSTN'T do that. For no obligation, the stress is often on “have”: You don't HAVE to.
erreurs: You don't have to pay. It's free.
Free = no need to pay, not a prohibition.
You don't have to smoke in the hospital.
You mustn't smoke in the hospital.
Yesterday I couldn't go out. / I wasn't allowed to go out.
Make the negative of have to with do.

dialogue.contexte: In a museum in Ottawa, a guard talks to two visitors from Douala, Linda and her son Ryan.
lignes: Good morning. Just so you know, you mustn't take photos with a flash.
OK. Do we have to leave our bags at the entrance?
Small bags are fine, so you don't have to leave yours. But you mustn't eat or drink in the galleries.
Do I have to pay? I'm twelve.
No, children under thirteen don't have to pay.
Great! Can I touch the dinosaur?
Sorry, you mustn't touch it. But you can touch the stones in room 4.

mots: you can choose to do it or not
English is compulsory at this school.
You need permission to film here.
when someone says you can do something
There's a warning on the door.
words that tell you about a danger
Leave your bag at the entrance.
the door or place where you go in
to put your hand on something
You can't park in front of the gate.
to leave a car in a place for a time
Don't tell anyone. It's a secret.
something that other people must not know

exercices.consigne: Does the sentence show a prohibition or no obligation?
items: You mustn't cross the road here.
prohibition
You don't have to wear a suit on Fridays.
no obligation
He doesn't have to cook tonight.
no obligation
Passengers mustn't stand near the doors.
prohibition

exercices.titre: 2. Mustn't or don't / doesn't have to?
items: It's a holiday tomorrow, so we ___ go to work.
don't have to
You ___ drive after drinking alcohol.
mustn't
The museum is free. You ___ buy a ticket.
don't have to
You ___ open this door. The alarm will ring.
mustn't
My brother ___ get up early. He works from home.
doesn't have to
You ___ forget your passport!
mustn't

exercices.consigne: Put the sentence in the past.
items: I don't have to wear a uniform.
I didn't have to wear a uniform.
We can't use our phones in the exam.
We couldn't use our phones in the exam.
She doesn't have to pay.
She didn't have to pay.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake in form or meaning. Write it correctly.
items: Breakfast is included, so you mustn't pay for it.
Breakfast is included, so you don't have to pay for it.
You don't have to swim here. It's dangerous!
You mustn't swim here. It's dangerous!
He don't have to come.
He doesn't have to come.
I haven't to study tonight.
I don't have to study tonight.

exercices.consigne: Rewrite with mustn't, don't have to or needn't.
items: It isn't necessary for you to answer.
You don't have to answer.
Don't forget the keys — it's very important!
You mustn't forget the keys. / We mustn't forget the keys.
It isn't necessary to bring a present.
You don't have to bring a present. / You needn't bring a present.

exercices.consigne: Write the rules of a place you know (your job, your school, your home): three prohibitions with mustn't / can't and two freedoms with don't have to.
items: Model answer

At my gym in Brussels, you mustn't use your phone on the machines. You can't enter without a card, and you mustn't leave your towel on the floor. But you don't have to book a time, and you don't have to pay extra for the classes.

a_retenir: don't / doesn't have to + base = not necessary (you can choose).
Prohibition also with can't or not allowed to; no obligation also with needn't / don't need to.
Past: couldn't / wasn't allowed to (prohibition); didn't have to (no obligation).
Free = You don't have to pay, never You mustn't pay.
